### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**16** anchor(s) derived from **3** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/utils/datetime.ts`, `packages/core/src/utils/temporal-comparand.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/calendar-day.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/utils/datetime.ts`, `packages/core/src/utils/temporal-comparand.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/calendar-day.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **7** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **142** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1741c5dcb62d11bc9b59702dd67080ef6a7ac9e8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `303dd621fc30a3d5d5a9274687418f2a2c4645ac` — the merge of head `a3afb404b6418eaa640f223e06d0ca5ed71286e0` into base `1741c5dcb62d11bc9b59702dd67080ef6a7ac9e8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 303dd621fc30a3d5d5a9274687418f2a2c4645ac && git checkout 303dd621fc30a3d5d5a9274687418f2a2c4645ac
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1741c5dcb62d11bc9b59702dd67080ef6a7ac9e8 a3afb404b6418eaa640f223e06d0ca5ed71286e0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1741c5dcb62d11bc9b59702dd67080ef6a7ac9e8 && git merge --no-ff a3afb404b6418eaa640f223e06d0ca5ed71286e0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1741c5dcb62d11bc9b59702dd67080ef6a7ac9e8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a3afb404b6418eaa640f223e06d0ca5ed71286e0`
Local-runs: none

PR #20843 on card #20280 (the `datetime` half; PR #20306 landed the `date` half). The head was `a3afb404b6418eaa640f223e06d0ca5ed71286e0` at both reads, draft, open. Inputs: the card's body and all eleven comments, #20264, the PR body, its 20-file list, the net diff against `main` at the merge base `b28054654d` (20 files, +560/−158), and the head's check-runs. Read-only: git reads of the fetched branch and REST reads; nothing built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on this head, read once just before this record was written:** 34 runs, 26 `success`, 3 `skipped`, 5 `in_progress`, 0 `failure`. `success`: `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Build Core`, `TypeScript Type Check` with `Type Check · workspace`, `· source gates`, `· consumer gates` and `· debt ledger`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` (three shards and the rollup), `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`, and the PR-shape checks (the card claims this branch; no other open PR claims the issue or the single-writer path; Part-of parity; PR size; documentation links; docs-affected flag). Still `in_progress`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Test Core (1/6)`, `(3/6)`, `(5/6)`, `(6/6)`. Not waited on.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept sets, door by door and spelling by spelling; each judged against the diff.

1. **The write door** (`record-validator.ts`, `VALIDATION_FAILED` with the field code `invalid_date`) narrows for a `datetime` field: a value whose UTC year falls in 0001..0999 was accepted at the base and is refused at the head, in every spelling the door read: an ISO instant string (with `Z`, an offset, or none), a bare `YYYY-MM-DD` (midnight UTC), a zone-naive `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM[:SS[.f]]` or `T` form, and a `Date`. A number was already refused (the arm's `readable` predicate admits only a `Date` or a `Date.parse`-readable string), so no number spelling moves. Reached on `engine.insert`, `engine.update` (one row or many) and `engine.validate`. Right: the validator's source diff is comment-only; it asks `isUninterpretableTemporalComparand`, which asks `isOutsideTemporalYearRange`, which now reads `FIRST_SUPPORTED_YEAR[kind]`: one per-kind bound, no dialect switch, no second edit to the range.
2. **The comparand door** (`temporal-comparand-door.ts`, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400) narrows for a `datetime` field at `where`, at a per-aggregation `filter` and at `having` (list-operator members included): a string the `datetime` rule reads, a `Date` and a number (epoch milliseconds) whose UTC year falls in 0001..0999 are refused before any driver read. Right: the door's diff moves words and classes only; the verdict stays core's predicate. Pinned at every position (`engine-temporal-year-range.test.ts`, and the `having` twin).
3. **REST** narrows through those two doors with no `packages/rest/src` change: `POST /api/v1/data/:object`, `PATCH …/:id`, each row of `POST …/import` (the reader layer is unchanged; the write door behind it refuses the row as `invalid_date`), and `POST …/query`. Right; pinned in the six REST test files.
4. **service-analytics' native-SQL decline**: `comparand-shape.ts` asks the same core predicate of every temporal literal, so `NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle` now declines a `datetime` comparand in 0001..0999 and the query is served on the engine path, where the door refuses it. Right; no source change in that package; read from source, as the PR says.
5. **The UTC year is the year judged**: the first instant of year 1000 at an offset of plus eight hours (year 999 in UTC) is refused; the last hour of year 999 at an offset of minus two hours (year 1000 in UTC) is read. Right; pinned on both doors.
6. **`date` is unchanged** on both doors: 0001..9999, padded to four digits from `FIRST_SUPPORTED_YEAR.date`. Right by construction (the `date` entry stays 1 and the padding reads that entry) and by the `date` controls added in every pin file. The `date` year-class sentences are byte-identical: the `misorders()` helper composes exactly the base template ("It would reach the driver in a form that does not sort as a day and answer the wrong rows, or a database error." and "Compared with each group, it does not sort as a day and would keep the wrong groups.").
7. **`time` is unchanged: the H2 fork.** `misreadClassOf` asked `isOutsideTemporalYearRange(value, 'datetime')` for a `time` hit and now asks `isInstantOutsideFourDigitYears`, which reads a string into the instant the `datetime` rule reads (`temporalStorageForm`) and asks core's `date` range of that instant; a number or a `Date` goes straight through. At the base the `datetime` range was 0001..9999; at the head the `date` range is 0001..9999, and both read a number, a `Date` or a string's instant by its UTC year, so every `time` answer is unchanged by reading. A `time` refusal's verdict never consulted the floor (the `time` predicate reads `keepsTimeOfDay`, which the floor does not touch), and its misread class keeps the four-digit years. The helper asks core's function and does no year arithmetic of its own; it borrows the `date` kind's bound as "the four-digit years", which its docblock says out loud. Consistent with the dev's 0 of 414 moved. Right.
8. **Words only, not accept sets**: `YEAR_CLASS` names 1000 to 9999 for a `datetime`; the new `DATETIME_BEFORE_YEAR_1000` class gives 0001..0999 its own consequence sentence (such a value sorts as the instant it names on every backend, so the base's "does not sort as an instant" would be false for it); year 0 and a year past 9999 keep the misorder words. A comparand in 0001..0999 already refused for its spelling or its day is now named by its year class first (the six the PR body counts). No tracker number in the runtime strings.
9. **Public surface**: nothing exported moves. `isOutsideTemporalYearRange` keeps its signature; `FIRST_SUPPORTED_YEAR` (now a per-kind record) and `isInstantOutsideFourDigitYears` are module-private; `temporalStorageForm` was already exported from core. The `packages/spec` change is one docblock sentence in `calendar-day.ts`. Right.
10. **Widening**: none. The only bound that moved went from 1 to 1000; nothing refused at the base is accepted at the head. The dev's corpus reads 0 refused-to-accepted, consistent with the source.
11. **Seat ruling 5859414357 C holds**: no mysql2 parser change. `driver-sql`'s source is untouched; its one changed file is the year-range test.

Triage's answer A (5905050200), item by item: a `datetime` below year 1000 refused at both doors: met. `date` keeps 0001..9999: met. One per-kind bound inside `isOutsideTemporalYearRange`, no dialect switch, no second edit: met. The existing refusal codes: met (`INVALID_FILTER`; `VALIDATION_FAILED` / `invalid_date`; no new code). "Naming the kind and the range": met at the comparand door; the write door names the kind and keeps its existing sentence (③ item 7). Pins: the `datetime` 0001..0999 controls flip to refused on both doors, 1000 and 9999 are accepted, `date` 0001..0999 stay accepted: met, in core, objectql, driver-memory, driver-sql and rest. A BREAKING `minor` with an ADR-0087 disposition: met (②).

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/20280-datetime-year-floor.md`: `@objectstack/core` `minor`, `@objectstack/objectql` `minor`, a `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`. Right: the launch-window convention ships an accept-set narrowing as `minor` with the banner as the carrier, and the two packages whose published source moves are the two graded. `rest` and `service-analytics` narrow through a dependency with no `src/**` change of their own and are named in the prose; under this repo's rule (WHICH LEVEL: the level follows the act on a package's own published surface, and the level axis judges only a declared clause ②) they need no frontmatter entry, the fixed group moves them in lockstep, and `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. Right.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is the line: the diff widens no surface and narrows two doors, which is the `no (narrowing)` arm of `clause2-line.mjs`; triage's `yes (narrowing)` spelling would have read as "widens one surface and narrows another", which this diff does not do. The PR body carries the same line.
- ADR-0087: exactly one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The body carries no FROM/TO table, no arrow and no migration heading (the only arrow-shaped bytes in the file are the marker's own closing delimiter). The category is right: the change refuses a value; no authorable key, spelling, export or stored metadata shape moves, so nothing exists for `objectstack migrate meta` to rewrite; a `datetime` stored below 1000 is record data, and the body says it is never shifted. The operator path in the body (a `$lt` census on the floor's first instant, then a write into the range or `null`) is guidance about data, not a rewrite of a consumer's code or metadata; the prescription refusal is about consumer rewrites, and the disposition triage asked for ("refused with guidance, never silently shifted") is exactly that paragraph.
- Review faces, sentence by sentence:
  - **The changeset**: every factual sentence read true, with two notes. The MySQL sentences are true by mechanism and by measurement: the century shift is mysql2's read presentation of 0001..0099 (from 0100 up MySQL reads a `DATETIME` back as written; card comment 5875809297), and the `$lt` census finds such rows "because the comparison runs on the stored value": the SQL `WHERE` compares the stored `DATETIME` literal, not the presented `Date`, which is what PR #20306's live rows showed (`$eq` on the written value found the year-9 `datetime` row at base and head). Not re-measured on this head: no live MySQL locally, and the REST file's MySQL cell is a local instrument by ruling 5859414357 B. A precision note, not a falsity: "or with `null`" holds for a field that is not `required`.
  - **The PR body**: one false sentence, in Acceptance notes: "Four REST test files went red and are rewritten above, plus one comment line in a fifth." The file list has six REST test files: five rewritten because they pinned a `datetime` below 1000 at the public door (`data-temporal-year-range`, `data-date-read-year-below-100`, `data-query-calendar-day-year-below-100`, `import-date-cell-iso-real-day`, `import-datetime-year-below-100`) and a comment-only sixth (`data-query-date-year-range`). The body's own pins section and the `os-dev-report` count all six; the sentence should read five and a sixth. A body edit, which does not move the head. Every other factual sentence read true, including "later commits are tests and the changeset" (no non-test source changed after `65728398b2`), the two eslint config lines cited, and the sentence on `Temporal Conformance` (that job runs the whole `driver-sql` suite with the live MySQL URL and the matrix expectation set, so the year-range file's new year-1000 row runs there).
  - **The refusal prose in `temporal-comparand-door.ts`**: true. The `datetime` year class names 1000 to 9999; the before-1000 sentence states MySQL's documented floor and the measured 0001..0099 misread and claims no misorder; the remedy names the range; the docblock's history matches what #20264 and #20280 measured.
  - **`packages/spec/src/data/calendar-day.ts`**: one docblock sentence, true (the years end at 9999; a `date` 0001..9999, a `datetime` 1000..9999; the doors refuse the rest). Declared in the PR body and in the report as the spec lane's file.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Five REST test files changed**: answered, right. REST source is untouched; the files pinned the two doors one layer out, at the public door, and had to move with them; the dispatch's pin surface named the inner packages and these are the same pins. The PR body's count is wrong by one (② above); the report's is right.
2. **`YEAR_CLASS` changed shape; `DATETIME_BEFORE_YEAR_1000` added; `date` refusals byte-identical**: answered, right, and confirmed by composing the templates (① item 6). The old single `misorder` template was false for a `datetime` in 0001..0999.
3. **The driver pins keep rows below 1000**: answered, right. Neither driver is a door (both file headers say the doors sit in the engine); the rows are the stored-before-floor class the disposition describes, written straight through the driver; headers corrected and a year-1000 edge row added in each; the MySQL cell still asserts the stored text for 0001..0099.
4. **One merge of `main`**: answered. The merge commit brings `b28054654d` in. `main` had moved one file of this diff since the dev's base `4b45afaed5`, `import-date-cell-iso-real-day.test.ts`, by #20722's `codeOf` change, and the merge combined both edits without conflict; the merged table is coherent (the new `dt` row below 1000 is refused as `invalid_date`, the code `codeOf` gives a `dt` cell). The net diff of the other 19 files has the same patch-id as the dev's pre-merge branch, byte for byte. The report's "touched no file of this diff" is inexact for that one file; the PR body's narrower claim (the merge left `temporal-storage-form.ts` at the same blob) is true. The dev's suites and gates ran at the merged head.
5. **`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:type-check-debt` NOT MEASURED locally**: answered from CI. `Build Core` hosts the first (its "Every published require entry point actually loads" step) and `Type Check · debt ledger` runs the second; both `success` on this head.
6. **Live MySQL NOT MEASURED locally**: answered from CI. `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is `success` on this head. It runs `pnpm --filter @objectstack/driver-sql test` against live PostgreSQL 16 and MySQL 8.0 with the matrix expectation set, so `sql-driver-20264-temporal-year-range.test.ts`, its year-1000 edge row and its MySQL stored-text cell ran there.
7. **`open_questions[0]`**: answered by the seat (5910336270): A in this PR, B filed as #20846. Judged only for the faces: A leaves no face sentence false. The changeset says the write refusal is the existing `invalid_date` sentence for a `datetime` field, and the PR body says the write door names the kind, not the range, and why. Triage's "naming the kind and the range" is met at the comparand door; the write door's range words are #20846's.
8. **The out-of-scope finding** (a relative-date placeholder resolving outside the four-digit years steps around the door): this diff does not touch that path. The placeholder step-around in `isUninterpretableTemporalComparand` (the `classifyFilterToken` exemption) and the door's position before token resolution are unchanged. Filed by the seat as #20844.
9. **Governed surfaces**: none in the file list (`.changeset` and `packages/**` only); `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is `success`.
10. **Before landing**: correct the PR body's REST file count (five rewritten and a comment-only sixth), a body edit that does not move this head; and read `Lint & Repo Gates` and the four remaining `Test Core` shards green, as the queue rule asks.
